title: Preliminary findings on the role of the mental health and wellbeing practitioner within a Psychological Therapies for Severe Mental Health Problems (PT-SMHP) service
abstract: Abstract It has long been recognised that there is a cohort of service users who typically fail to meet criteria for specialist secondary mental health services, yet their needs are considered too complex for Talking Therapies services. As a result, new psychological practitioner roles, including mental health and wellbeing practitioners (MHWP), were introduced to support implementation efforts, including for newly commissioned Psychological Therapies for Severe Mental Health Problems (PT-SMHP) programmes. This study aimed to explore the impact of the newly commissioned MHWP role’s deliverance of low-intensity CBT-informed interventions on service user outcome measures across three time points during psychological intervention within a primary care-based PT-SMHP service in the East of England. Repeated measures-ANOVAs found significant improvement in all outcome measures, and further post-hoc pairwise comparisons generally found significant improvements in measures across each of the three time points. These preliminary findings provide initial evidence that the role of MHWPs are making a difference in community-based primary care services and positively impacting service user outcomes. Further studies are needed to investigate efficacy of the role with a larger sample, including across other mental health settings such as secondary care to ensure external validity. Key learning aims (1) To introduce the role of a mental health and wellbeing practitioner in a primary care-based psychological therapy service for severe mental health difficulties. (2) To examine preliminary outcomes of mental health and wellbeing practitioners in the treatment of individuals presenting with a personality disorder. (3) To consider what further research may be needed in relation to the mental health and wellbeing practitioner role.
